correctness.rationale: For every real box the exact minima follow from the even-coordinate-sum lattice rank obstruction and the vectors 2e1, e1±e2, e1+ej; all thresholds and ties are accounted for. Parity-character enumeration gives an exact integer point formula with strict interior conventions. Algebra then gives an exact rational signed defect for all integer boxes and an exhaustive sign/equality split; monotonicity and an explicit root inequality prove the continuous isotropic failure bands. The 274 test cases corroborate but do not substitute for the proof.

Freyer–Lucas Proposition 1.5 proves the product lower bound for symmetric lattice polygons; its other major results are broader but differently directed upper and weaker interior bounds.
Berg–Henk 2015 studies upper lattice-point bounds for bodies with centroid at the origin, not this lower-product sign classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a global upper bound nor the weaker linear interior lower bound implies the sign of the difference from the stronger (false) product lower bound for this special family. The two-dimensional theorem is consistent with, but does not cover, the new all-dimensional classification.

value.rationale: The 2026 counterexample asks naturally where the failed lower-product inequality is nonetheless valid. The new formula completely partitions all integer axis-box parameters into failure, equality and strict-validity regions, gives a sharp half-lattice-point additive correction, and shows that higher-dimensional failures occur even when the isotropic even-dimensional family is safe. The precise real-scale failure intervals and their decay rate offer a genuinely structural geometric boundary, not an arbitrary finite instance.
